magicWords.tip: Use when asking for anything: 'Coffee beku'.
Use for price, time, or quantity.
Add after any place: 'Bus stand ellide?'
Useful when someone asks you something.

slang.meaning: Buddy, friend, or bro (used casually between peers)
slang.example: ಏನ್ ಸಮಾಚಾರ ಗುರು? (En samaachara guru? - What's up buddy?)
ಮಚ್ಚಾ, ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯೋಣ ಬಾ! (Macha, coffee kudiyona baa!)
ಈ ದೋಸೆ ಸಕ್ಕತ್ ಆಗಿದೆ! (Ee dose sakkath aagide! - This dosa is awesome!)
ಊಟ ಬೊಂಬಾಟ್ ಗುರು! (Oota bombat guru! - The food is fantastic!)

slang.meaning: Please cooperate / adjust a little (The golden Bangalore phrase)
slang.example: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡಿ ಅಣ್ಣ (Swalpa adjust maadi anna)
ಏನೂ ತೊಂದರೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಸೀನ್ ಇಲ್ಲ ಬಿಡಿ! (Scene illa bidi!)

slang.meaning: Respectful address for strangers, shopkeepers, or drivers
Elder brother / Elder sister (essential friendly honorific)

phrases.english: Does this bus go to Majestic?
phrases.whenToUse: Ask the conductor or waiting passengers before boarding any BMTC / KSRTC bus.
phrases.culturalTip: BMTC buses show destination boards in Kannada; asking this will save you from boarding the wrong route.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ಹತ್ತಿ (Haudu, hatti - Yes, get in) OR ಇಲ್ಲ, ಬೇರೆ ಬಸ್ ಬರುತ್ತೆ (Illa, bere bus barutthe - No, another bus will come)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು, ಒಂದು ಟಿಕೆಟ್ ಕೊಡಿ (Dhanyavaadagalu, ondu ticket kodi - Thank you, give one ticket)

phrases.english: Please come by the meter, sir / brother.
phrases.whenToUse: When hiring an auto-rickshaw anywhere in Bangalore or Mysore.
phrases.culturalTip: Addressing the driver politely as 'Anna' (brother) establishes immediate goodwill and prevents overcharging.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮೀಟರ್ ಮೇಲೆ 20 ರೂಪಾಯಿ ಕೊಡಿ (Meter mele 20 rupaayi kodi - Give 20 rs extra above meter)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ ಅಣ್ಣ, ಬನ್ನಿ (Sari anna, banni - Okay brother, let's go) OR ಇಲ್ಲ ಅಣ್ಣ, ಮೀಟರ್ ಅಷ್ಟೇ (Illa anna, meter ashte - No brother, only meter fare)

phrases.english: Stop here please, I need to get down.
phrases.whenToUse: Say this to an auto driver, cab driver, or bus driver when your stop arrives.
phrases.culturalTip: Short and clear. You can also simply say 'Illi nillisi anna' (Stop here, brother).

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಸರಿ, ಇಳಿರಿ (Sari, iliri - Okay, get down)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಎಷ್ಟು ಆಯ್ತು? (Eshtu aaythu? - How much did it come to?)

phrases.english: What is the next stop / station?
phrases.whenToUse: Ask fellow commuters inside a bus or metro train when you are unsure of your location.
phrases.culturalTip: Kannadigas are very helpful to commuters; someone will happily alert you when your stop arrives.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮುಂದಿನ ಸ್ಟಾಪ್ ಇಂದಿರಾನಗರ (Mundina stop Indiranagar - Next stop is Indiranagar)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಬಂದಾಗ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೇಳಿ (Bandaaga swalpa heli - Please let me know when it arrives)

phrases.english: How do I reach the metro station?
phrases.whenToUse: Ask pedestrians or shopkeepers when walking in unfamiliar neighborhoods.
phrases.culturalTip: People will guide you using landmarks like temples, circles, or flyovers.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮುಂದೆ ಹೋಗಿ, ಎಡಕ್ಕೆ ತಿರುಗಿ (Munde hogi, edakke thirugi - Go straight, turn left)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು! (Dhanyavaadagalu! - Thank you!)

phrases.english: How far is it from here?
phrases.whenToUse: Deciding whether to walk or hail an auto.
phrases.culturalTip: If they say 'Hathira' (ಹತ್ತಿರ), it's walkable (within 500m-1km).

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹತ್ತಿರನೇ ಇದೆ, ಹತ್ತು ನಿಮಿಷ ವಾಕ್ (Hattirane ide, hattu nimisha walk - It is a 10 min walk)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ, ನಡೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ (Sari, nadedukondu hogteeni - Alright, I will walk)

phrases.english: Turn right, then go straight.
phrases.whenToUse: Guiding a cab driver, auto driver, or a friend.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Balakke' = Right, 'Edakke' = Left, 'Neravaagi' = Straight.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಆಯಿತು ಸರ್ (Aayithu sir - Done sir)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಅಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ (Alli nillisi - Stop right there)

phrases.english: I need to go to the airport (Kempegowda International Airport).
phrases.whenToUse: Boarding a Vayu Vajra KIA bus or telling a taxi driver.
phrases.culturalTip: Vayu Vajra buses connect every part of Bangalore to KIA smoothly 24/7.

nextReply.theyMightSay: KIA-8 ಬಸ್ ಹತ್ತಿ (KIA-8 bus hatti - Board the KIA-8 bus)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಟಿಕೆಟ್ ದರ ಎಷ್ಟು? (Ticket dara eshtu? - What is the ticket fare?)

phrases.kannada: ಒಂದು ಮಸಾಲೆ ದೋಸೆ ಮತ್ತು ಒಂದು ಫಿಲ್ಟರ್ ಕಾಫಿ ಕೊಡಿ
phrases.english: One masala dosa and one filter coffee please.
phrases.pronunciation: ON-du ma-SAA-le DO-se mat-te ON-du FILTER COFFEE KO-di
phrases.whenToUse: The quintessential Bangalore Darshini breakfast order at the token counter.
phrases.culturalTip: Say 'kodi' (please give). Darshinis take orders at the cash counter first to issue a token.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಎಂಭತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ, ಸ್ಕ್ಯಾನ್ ಮಾಡಿ (Embatthu rupaayi, scan maadi - Eighty rupees, please scan)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸ್ಕ್ಯಾನ್ ಮಾಡಿದೆ, ಟೋಕನ್ ಕೊಡಿ (Scan maadide, token kodi - Scanned, give token)

phrases.english: Please make it less spicy.
phrases.whenToUse: Ordering dishes like Bisi Bele Bath, Chitranna, or Curries if sensitive to spices.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Khara' means spicy heat. 'Kammi maadi' politely asks to tone it down.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಸರಿ ಸರ್, ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಖಾರ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ (Sari sir, kammi khaara maadtivi - Okay, we will make it mild)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (Dhanyavaada - Thank you)

phrases.kannada: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಚಟ್ನಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಂಬಾರ್ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಹಾಕಿ
phrases.english: Please add a little more chutney and sambar.
phrases.pronunciation: SWAL-pa CHUTNEY mat-te SAMBAR JAAS-ti HAA-ki
phrases.whenToUse: At the serving counter in Darshinis where chutney refills are happily provided.
phrases.culturalTip: Bangalore coconut chutney and slightly sweet Udupi sambar refills are universally welcomed.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹಾಕ್ತೀನಿ, ಪ್ಲೇಟ್ ಮುಂದೆ ತನ್ನಿ (Haaktini, plate munde tanni - Bringing plate forward)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸಾಕು, ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು (Saaku, dhanyavaadagalu - That is enough, thank you)

phrases.english: Please give hot drinking water.
phrases.whenToUse: Asking waiter or counter boy for warm water.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Bisi neeru' = hot water, 'Tampu neeru' = cold water.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ ಸ್ವಾಮಿ (Tagolli swamy - Take it sir)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (Dhanyavaada - Thank you)

phrases.english: Can you pack this for takeaway / parcel?
phrases.whenToUse: Ordering food to take home or packaging leftovers.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Parcel' is standard throughout Karnataka restaurants.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ಕವರ್ ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಐದು ರೂಪಾಯಿ (Haudu, cover charge aidu rupaayi - Yes, packaging is 5 rs)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ, ಪ್ಯಾಕ್ ಮಾಡಿ (Sari, pack maadi - Okay, please pack it)

phrases.english: The food is very delicious / good!
phrases.whenToUse: Complimenting the cook, waiter, or host after a meal.
phrases.culturalTip: A heartfelt 'Oota chennagide' brings an instant, proud smile to any cook or restaurant owner.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ತುಂಬಾ ಸಂತೋಷ ಸರ್, ಮತ್ತೆ ಬನ್ನಿ (Tumba santhosha sir, matte banni - Very glad, come again!)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಖಂಡಿತ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ (Khanditha bartini - Definitely will come)

phrases.english: How much rupees is this?
phrases.whenToUse: The quintessential shopping question at any vegetable stall, bakery, or street shop.
phrases.culturalTip: You can also simply point and ask 'Idhu eshtu?' (How much is this?).

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಐವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ (Aivatthu rupaayi - Fifty rupees)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಅಣ್ಣ (Swalpa kammi maadi anna - Please reduce a little bit, brother)

phrases.english: Please reduce the price a little, brother.
phrases.whenToUse: Polite street bargaining at local markets like KR Market, Malleshwaram 8th Cross, or Commercial Street.
phrases.culturalTip: Always smile and say 'Kammi maadi'. Aggressive bargaining is discouraged, but friendly requests always work.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಸರಿ, ನಲವತ್ತಕ್ಕೆ ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ (Sari, nalavattak-ke tagolli - Okay, take it for forty)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ಕೊಡಿ (Dhanyavaada, kodi - Thank you, give it)

phrases.english: Do you accept UPI / PhonePe / Google Pay?
phrases.whenToUse: Before purchasing at small street vendors, coconut vendors, or tea stalls.
phrases.culturalTip: Bangalore is India's tech hub; 99% of roadside vendors have a QR soundbox, but it's polite to ask.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ಕ್ಯೂಆರ್ ಕೋಡ್ ಸ್ಕ್ಯಾನ್ ಮಾಡಿ (Haudu, QR code scan maadi - Yes, scan the QR code)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಪೇ ಮಾಡಿದೆ, ನೋಡಿ (Pay maadide, nodi - I have paid, please check)

phrases.kannada: ಒಂದು ಕೆಜಿ ತಾಜಾ ಹಣ್ಣು / ತರಕಾರಿ ಕೊಡಿ
phrases.english: Give me one kilogram of fresh fruits / vegetables.
phrases.pronunciation: ON-du KG TAA-jaa HAN-nu / ta-ra-KAA-ri KO-di
phrases.whenToUse: Ordering at local vegetable and fruit markets.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Taaja' means fresh. Saying 'Ondu kg kodi' is clear and polite.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಇನ್ನೇನು ಬೇಕು? (In-ne-nu beku? - What else do you need?)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಸಾಕು, ಬಿಲ್ ಎಷ್ಟು? (Ashte saaku, bill eshtu? - That is enough, what is the bill?)

phrases.english: Do you have change with you?
phrases.whenToUse: When handing over a 500-rupee note for a 40-rupee purchase.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Chillare' is the universal word across Karnataka for small change / coins.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಇಲ್ಲ, ಆನ್‌ಲೈನ್ ಪೇ ಮಾಡಿ (Illa, online pay maadi - No, please pay online)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ, PhonePe ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ (Sari, PhonePe maadtini - Okay, I will do PhonePe)

phrases.english: Do you have another colour or size?
phrases.whenToUse: Clothing and footwear shopping.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Banna' = colour; 'Bere' = another / different.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ನೀಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕಪ್ಪು ಇದೆ (Haudu, neeli matte kappu ide - Yes, blue and black are available)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ನೀಲಿ ಬಣ್ಣ ತೋರಿಸಿ (Neeli banna thorisi - Show me the blue colour)

phrases.kannada: ನನಗೆ ಜ್ವರ ಮತ್ತು ತಲೆ ನೋವು ಇದೆ
phrases.english: I have fever and a headache.
phrases.pronunciation: NA-na-ge JVA-ra mat-te TA-le NO-vu I-de
phrases.whenToUse: Explaining symptoms to a doctor or pharmacist.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Jvara' = fever, 'Tale novu' = headache, 'Hotte novu' = stomachache.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಎಷ್ಟು ದಿನದಿಂದ ಇದೆ? (Eshtu dinadinda ide? - Since how many days?)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಎರಡು ದಿನದಿಂದ (Eradu dinadinda - Since two days)

phrases.english: Where is the nearest hospital or clinic?
phrases.whenToUse: Urgent healthcare situation when looking for medical attention.
phrases.culturalTip: Aaspatre is the Kannada word for hospital. Anyone will immediately direct you.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮುಂದಿನ ಜಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ ಇದೆ (Mundina junction-nalli dodda aaspatre ide)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ಬೇಗ ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ (Dhanyavaada, bega hogteeni - Thank you, I will go quickly)

phrases.english: Should I take this medicine after food?
phrases.whenToUse: Clarifying dosage instructions with a chemist or doctor.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Ootada nantara' = after food, 'Ootakkinta munche' = before food.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ರಾತ್ರಿ ಊಟದ ನಂತರ ಒಂದು ಮಾತ್ರೆ (Haudu, raatri ootada nantara ondu maatre)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ, ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು (Sari, arthavaayithu - Okay, I understood)

phrases.english: When will the doctor arrive?
phrases.whenToUse: Inquiring at a clinic reception desk.
phrases.culturalTip: Doctors are addressed respectfully as 'Vaidyaru' or 'Doctor-re'.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಸಂಜೆ ಐದು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಬರ್ತಾರೆ (Sanje aidu gantege bartare - Doctor arrives at 5 PM)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಟೋಕನ್ ನಂಬರ್ ಕೊಡಿ (Token number kodi - Please give the token number)

phrases.english: I am allergic to this medicine.
phrases.whenToUse: Crucial safety phrase during doctor consultation.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Aushadhi' is medicine. Informing the doctor about allergies prevents medical mishaps.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಬೇರೆ ಔಷಧಿ ಬರೆದುಕೊಡ್ತೀನಿ (Bere aushadhi baredhu kodteeni - I will prescribe an alternative medicine)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು (Tumba dhanyavaadagalu - Thank you very much)

phrases.kannada: ಮನೆ ಅಥವಾ ಪಿಜಿ ಬಾಡಿಗೆಗೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಇದೆಯಾ?
phrases.english: Is a house or PG room vacant for rent?
phrases.pronunciation: MA-ne a-tha-va PG BAA-di-ge-ge KHAA-li I-de-yaa?
phrases.whenToUse: Calling a to-let board number or inquiring with building security.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Baadige' means rent; 'Khaali' means vacant. Essential for house hunters in Karnataka.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, 1 BHK ಖಾಲಿ ಇದೆ (Haudu, 1 BHK khaali ide - Yes, 1 BHK is vacant)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ತಿಂಗಳಿಗೆ ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅಡ್ವಾನ್ಸ್ ಎಷ್ಟು? (Tingalige baadige matte advance eshtu? - How much rent and deposit?)

phrases.kannada: ತಿಂಗಳಿಗೆ ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅಡ್ವಾನ್ಸ್ ಡಿಪಾಸಿಟ್ ಎಷ್ಟು?
phrases.english: What is the monthly rent and advance deposit?
phrases.pronunciation: TIN-ga-li-ge BAA-di-ge mat-te ADVANCE DEPOSIT ESH-tu?
phrases.whenToUse: Clarifying financial terms with the landlord.
phrases.culturalTip: In Bangalore, security deposits vary from 2 to 6 months' rent. Asking early is crucial.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಹದಿನೈದು ಸಾವಿರ, ಅಡ್ವಾನ್ಸ್ ಐವತ್ತು ಸಾವಿರ (Rent 15k, advance 50k)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಮೇಂಟೆನೆನ್ಸ್ ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿದ್ದೆಯಾ? (Maintenance idaralli seriddheya? - Is maintenance included?)

phrases.kannada: ಕಾವೇರಿ ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಸೌಲಭ್ಯ ಇದೆಯಾ?
phrases.english: Is there Cauvery water and electricity facility?
phrases.pronunciation: CAUVERY NEE-ru mat-te VID-yut SAU-la-bhya I-de-yaa?
phrases.whenToUse: Crucial infrastructure check for house hunting in Bangalore.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Cauvery neeru' indicates municipal water supply, which is superior to borewell-only tankers.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ದಿನದ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ನಾಲ್ಕು ಗಂಟೆ ನೀರು ಬರುತ್ತೆ (Yes, 24 hours water comes)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ತುಂಬಾ ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು (Tumba olleyadu - Very good)

phrases.english: What time will the meeting start?
phrases.whenToUse: Checking schedule with coworkers or managers.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Eshtu hottige' means 'at what time'. Common daily corporate phrase.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ (Madhyaahna mooru gantege - At 3 PM in the afternoon)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಸರಿ, ಲಿಂಕ್ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿ (Sari, link kaluhisi - Okay, please send the link)

phrases.english: Come, let's go have tea or coffee.
phrases.whenToUse: The quintessential Bangalore office break icebreaker at 4 PM.
phrases.culturalTip: Filter coffee breaks are where strong team bonds and friendships are forged in Karnataka.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು ಬನ್ನಿ, ಒಂದು ಬ್ರೇಕ್ ಬೇಕಾಗಿತ್ತು (Haudu banni, ondu break bekaagittu)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಟೀ ಸ್ಟಾಲ್‌ಗೆ ಹೋಗೋಣ (Hattirada tea stall ge hogona)

phrases.english: Please send this file or document.
phrases.whenToUse: Requesting project resources from teammates.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Kaluhisi' is polite for 'please send'.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಈಗಲೇ ಇಮೇಲ್ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ (Eegale email maadtini - I will email it right now)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (Tumba dhanyavaada - Thank you very much)

phrases.english: Sir / Madam, may I come in?
phrases.whenToUse: Polite permission before entering a lecture hall or staff room.
phrases.culturalTip: Universities and schools in Karnataka value polite entry etiquette.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಬನ್ನಿ, ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ (Banni, kootkolli - Come in, have a seat)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು ಸರ್ (Dhanyavaadagalu sir - Thank you sir)

phrases.english: Where is the library located?
phrases.whenToUse: Campus navigation for new students.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Granthalaya' is the formal Kannada word; both 'Library' and 'Granthalaya' are understood.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮೊದಲನೇ ಮಹಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೆ (Modalane mahadiyalli ide - On the first floor)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಟೈಮಿಂಗ್ಸ್ ಏನು? (Timings enu? - What are the library timings?)

phrases.kannada: ಹೊಸ ಖಾತೆ ತೆರೆಯಲು ಈ ಫಾರ್ಮ್ ತುಂಬಬೇಕಾ?
phrases.english: Should I fill this form to open a new account?
phrases.pronunciation: HO-sa KHAA-te te-RE-ya-lu ee FORM TUM-ba-BE-kaa?
phrases.whenToUse: At bank help desks or public service counters.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Khaate' = account. Officials will point to specific columns to sign.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಹೌದು, ಆಧಾರ್ ಕಾರ್ಡ್ ಜೆರಾಕ್ಸ್ ಕೊಡಿ (Haudu, Aadhaar card xerox kodi)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಜೆರಾಕ್ಸ್ ಇದೆ, ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ (Xerox ide, tagolli - I have the copy, take it)

phrases.english: What is the token counter number?
phrases.whenToUse: Public offices, post offices, and RTO counters.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Counter number' is universally understood.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮೂರನೇ ಕೌಂಟರ್ ಗೆ ಹೋಗಿ (Moorane counter ge hogi - Go to counter 3)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (Dhanyavaada - Thank you)

phrases.english: Hello / Greetings! What is your name?
phrases.whenToUse: Polite introduction with new neighbors, colleagues, or acquaintances.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Namaskara' with folded hands is the timeless Kannada greeting.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ಸುರೇಶ್, ನಿಮ್ಮದು? (Nanna hesaru Suresh, nimmadu?)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... ಭೇಟಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದು ಖುಷಿಯಾಯಿತು (Nanna hesaru... Bhetiyaagiddu khushiyaayithu - Nice to meet you)

phrases.english: Did you have food? / Have you eaten?
phrases.whenToUse: The ultimate cultural warmth phrase in Karnataka. Asking this is like asking 'How are you?'
phrases.culturalTip: Asking 'Oota aaytha?' shows genuine care and affection across friends, neighbors, and colleagues.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಆಯ್ತು, ನಿಮ್ಮದು ಆಯ್ತಾ? (Aaythu, nimmadu aaytha? - Yes done, what about yours?)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ನನ್ನದು ಆಯ್ತು, ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು (Nannadu aaythu, dhanyavaadagalu - Mine is done too, thank you)

phrases.english: Happy Kannada Rajyotsava (Karnataka Formation Day)!
phrases.whenToUse: November 1st and throughout Karnataka Rajyotsava month.
phrases.culturalTip: Wishing locals on Rajyotsava displays immense cultural respect and affection for Karnataka.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ನಿಮಗೂ ಕೂಡ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು! (Nimagu kooda shubhaashayagalu! - Greetings to you too!)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಜೈ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಮಾತೆ! (Jai Karnataka Maate!)

phrases.english: Please help me!
phrases.whenToUse: Urgent distress or when you need someone's immediate attention.
phrases.culturalTip: 'Dayavittu' adds deep politeness, signaling genuine need.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಏನಾಯ್ತು? ಏನು ಸಹಾಯ ಬೇಕು? (Enaaythu? Enu sahaaya beku? - What happened? What help is needed?)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ನನಗೆ ಈ ಜಾಗ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (Nanage ee jaaga gottilla - I do not know this place)

phrases.kannada: ನನ್ನ ದಾರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿದೆ, ಈ ವಿಳಾಸ ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ?
phrases.english: I have lost my way, where is this address?
phrases.pronunciation: NAN-na DAA-ri TAP-pi-de, ee vi-LAA-sa EL-li-de?
phrases.whenToUse: When lost in an unfamiliar locality or trying to find a house number.
phrases.culturalTip: Show the address text on your phone alongside saying this phrase.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ತೋರಿಸಿ, ನಾನು ಮಾರ್ಗ ತೋರಿಸ್ತೀನಿ (Thorisi, naanu maarga thoristini - Show me, I will show the path)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ತುಂಬಾ ಉಪಕಾರ! (Tumba upakaara! - Immense favor/thanks!)

phrases.kannada: ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಬರಲ್ಲ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ
phrases.english: I don't know Kannada properly, please speak slowly.
phrases.pronunciation: NA-na-ge Kan-na-da sa-ri-YAA-gi BA-ral-la, SWAL-pa ni-DHAA-na-vaa-gi maa-tha-NAA-di
phrases.whenToUse: When someone speaks too fast or uses complex dialect.
phrases.culturalTip: Kannadigas appreciate learners and will instantly shift to simpler words or English.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ! ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಹೇಳ್ತೀನಿ (Paravaagilla! Nidhaanavaagi heltini - No problem! I will tell you slowly)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು (Dhanyavaadagalu - Thank you)

phrases.english: Where is the nearest police station?
phrases.whenToUse: In case of theft, lost documents, or seeking police protection.
phrases.culturalTip: Police station is called 'Police Thaane' throughout Karnataka.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಮೇನ್ ರೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ ಸಿಗ್ನಲ್ ಪಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲೇ ಇದೆ (Main road-nalli traffic signal pakkadalle ide)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (Dhanyavaada - Thank you)

phrases.english: Please call an ambulance immediately (108).
phrases.whenToUse: Severe medical distress or critical road accident.
phrases.culturalTip: 108 is Karnataka's dedicated emergency ambulance helpline number.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ಈಗಲೇ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ (Eegale call maadtini - I am calling right now)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಬೇಗ ಬನ್ನಿ (Bega banni - Come quickly please)

phrases.english: Please give some drinking water.
phrases.whenToUse: Feeling dehydrated, exhausted, or unwell on the road.
phrases.culturalTip: In Karnataka culture, offering water is considered sacred; any shop or home will readily offer clean water.

nextReply.theyMightSay: ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ, ಕುಡಿಯಿರಿ (Tagolli, kudiyiri - Take it, drink)
nextReply.whatToSayNext: ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು ಅಣ್ಣ (Dhanyavaadagalu anna - Thank you brother)

dialogues.title: Hailing an Auto at Majestic
dialogues.scenario: You just arrived at Majestic station and need to hire an auto to Indiranagar with meter fare.

steps.speaker: Auto Driver
steps.english: Where do you want to go, sir?

options.english: To Indiranagar, will you put the meter, brother?
options.feedback: Perfect! Polite, respectful, and sets clear expectation for meter fare.
Too blunt and disrespectful. Always use polite speech with drivers.

steps.speaker: Auto Driver
steps.kannada: ಮೀಟರ್ ಮೇಲೆ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಕೊಡಿ ಸ್ವಾಮಿ, ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ ಇದೆ.
steps.pronunciation: Meter mele IP-pat-tu roo-PAA-yi jaas-ti KO-di swaami, traffic i-de.
steps.english: Give twenty rupees extra above meter sir, there is heavy traffic.

options.feedback: Great compromise! 20 rupees above meter is reasonable during peak hours.

options.english: No brother, I will only pay the meter amount.
options.feedback: Also valid! Assertive yet polite stance.

steps.speaker: You (Arrived at destination)
steps.english: Stop right here brother, how much did it come to?

options.kannada: PhonePe / UPI ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ, ಕ್ಯೂಆರ್ ಕೋಡ್ ತೋರಿಸಿ.
options.pronunciation: PhonePe / UPI maadtini, QR code thorisi.
options.english: I will do PhonePe / UPI, show the QR code.
options.feedback: Spot on! The modern Bangalore way to pay seamlessly.

dialogues.title: Ordering Breakfast at a Bangalore Darshini
dialogues.scenario: You walk into an iconic Darshini (like Taaza Thindi or CTR) for morning breakfast.

options.kannada: ಒಂದು ಮಸಾಲೆ ದೋಸೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಒಂದು ಫಿಲ್ಟರ್ ಕಾಫಿ ಕೊಡಿ.
options.pronunciation: Ondu masale dose matte ondu filter coffee kodi.
options.english: One masala dosa and one filter coffee please.

options.feedback: Grammatically crude. Always specify the item and use 'kodi' (please give).

options.english: I have scanned, see here, please give the token.
options.feedback: Excellent! Next step is collecting your fresh hot dosa at the kitchen counter.

dialogues.title: At the Local Pharmacy
dialogues.scenario: You have a seasonal sore throat and mild fever and need medication.

steps.speaker: Pharmacist
steps.english: Tell me sir, what is the trouble?

options.kannada: ನನಗೆ ಎರಡು ದಿನದಿಂದ ಗಂಟಲು ನೋವು ಮತ್ತು ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ.
options.pronunciation: Nanage eradu dinadinda gantalu novu matte jvara ide.
options.english: I have had a sore throat and fever for two days.
options.feedback: Accurately articulates duration and symptoms clearly.

steps.speaker: Pharmacist
steps.kannada: ಈ ಮಾತ್ರೆ ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ, ಊಟದ ನಂತರ ತಗೋಬೇಕು.
steps.pronunciation: Ee MAAT-re ta-GOL-li, OO-ta-da NAN-ta-ra ta-go-BE-ku.
steps.english: Take this tablet, you must take it after food.

options.english: How many times a day should I take it?
options.feedback: Vital question! Clarifies dosage frequency safely.

dialogues.title: House Hunting: Inquiring with Landlord
dialogues.scenario: You spot a To-Let board in Koramangala and call the owner to inquire about a 1BHK apartment.

options.kannada: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ ಸರ್, ಟು-ಲೆಟ್ ಬೋರ್ಡ್ ನೋಡಿ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡಿದೆ. 1 BHK ಖಾಲಿ ಇದೆಯಾ?
options.pronunciation: Namaskara sir, To-Let board nodi call maadide. 1 BHK khaali ideyaa?
options.english: Greetings sir, I called seeing the To-Let board. Is the 1 BHK vacant?
options.feedback: Professional, courteous, and gets straight to the point.

steps.speaker: House Owner
steps.kannada: ಹೌದು ಖಾಲಿ ಇದೆ. ನೀವು ಫ್ಯಾಮಿಲಿನಾ ಅಥವಾ ಬ್ಯಾಚುಲರ್ಸ್ ಆ?
steps.pronunciation: Haudu khaali ide. Neevu family-naa athava bachelors aa?
steps.english: Yes it is vacant. Are you a family or bachelors?

options.kannada: ನಾವು ಸಾಫ್ಟ್‌ವೇರ್ ಕಂಪನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ, ಫ್ಯಾಮಿಲಿ ಸರ್.
options.pronunciation: Naavu software company-nalli kelasa maadtivi, family sir.
options.english: We work at a software company, family sir.
options.feedback: Perfect! Mentions professional background and reassurance.

quizzes.situation: You are standing at a busy bus stop and a red BMTC bus arrives. You want to ask if it heads toward Electronic City.
quizzes.question: Which Kannada phrase should you use?
options: ಈ ಬಸ್ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನಿಕ್ ಸಿಟಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾ? (Ee bus Electronic City ge hoguttaa?)
ನನಗೆ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನಿಕ್ ಸಿಟಿ ಇಷ್ಟ (Nanage Electronic City ishta)
quizzes.explanation: 'Ee bus [place] ge hoguttaa?' is the universal question to check bus destinations before boarding.

quizzes.situation: You buy fresh mangoes at Malleshwaram market. The vendor quotes 150 rupees, but you want to politely ask for a slight reduction.
quizzes.question: What is the polite phrase to request a small discount?
options: ತುಂಬಾ ದುಬಾರಿ, ನಾನು ತಗೊಳಲ್ಲ (Tumba dubaari, naanu tagolalla)
ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಅಣ್ಣ (Swalpa kammi maadi anna)
quizzes.explanation: 'Swalpa kammi maadi anna' is respectful and universally effective across Karnataka markets.

quizzes.situation: You are at a local cafe and finished your meal. You don't have cash and want to pay digitally.
quizzes.question: How do you ask if they accept PhonePe or Google Pay?
quizzes.explanation: 'UPI / PhonePe tagotheeraa?' is the standard way to ask if digital QR payment is accepted.

quizzes.situation: You are feeling unwell with a high temperature and visit a clinic.
quizzes.question: What does 'Nanage jvara ide' (ನನಗೆ ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ) mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'Jvara' (ಜ್ವರ) translates directly to fever in Kannada.

quizzes.situation: A local elder speaks very quickly in Kannada and you cannot follow.
quizzes.question: Which phrase asks them politely to slow down?
quizzes.explanation: 'Nidhaanavaagi' means slowly. 'Dayavittu nidhaanavaagi maathanaadi' is extremely courteous.

quizzes.situation: You enter an auto-rickshaw and want to insist on lawful metering rather than flat price gouging.
quizzes.question: What is the key phrase?
options: ಮೀಟರ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಬನ್ನಿ ಸರ್ (Meter prakara banni sir)
quizzes.explanation: 'Meter prakara banni' directly tells the driver to commute according to the government meter.

quizzes.situation: You want to say 'Did you have food?' as a warm gesture of care to a coworker.
quizzes.question: What is Karnataka's most famous everyday cultural phrase?
quizzes.explanation: 'Oota aaytha?' (Did you have food?) is the supreme Kannada expression of friendship and care.

quizzes.situation: What does the popular Bangalore phrase 'Sakkath' (ಸಕ್ಕತ್) mean?
quizzes.question: Translate 'Sakkath' into English:
quizzes.explanation: 'Sakkath' means awesome, fantastic, or superb (e.g. 'Sakkath coffee!').

visualCards.english: Does this bus go to Majestic?

visualCards.title: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ
visualCards.subtitle: Stop Here
visualCards.english: Stop here brother, I need to get down

visualCards.title: PhonePe / GPay

visualCards.english: Do you accept PhonePe / Google Pay?

visualCards.title: ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಮಾಡಿ
visualCards.subtitle: Reduce Price
visualCards.english: Please reduce price a little, brother

visualCards.title: ಜ್ವರದ ಮಾತ್ರೆ
visualCards.subtitle: Fever Medicine
visualCards.audioText: ಜ್ವರ ಮತ್ತು ತಲೆನೋವು ಇದೆ, ಮಾತ್ರೆ ಕೊಡಿ
visualCards.pronounce: Jvara matte talenovu ide, maatre kodi
visualCards.english: I have fever and headache, give medicine

visualCards.title: ತುರ್ತು ಸಹಾಯ!
visualCards.subtitle: Emergency Help!
visualCards.audioText: ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿ! ನನಗೆ ತೊಂದರೆ ಆಗಿದೆ!
visualCards.pronounce: Dayavittu sahaaya maadi! Nanage tondare aagide!
visualCards.english: Please help me! I am in emergency trouble!

visualCards.english: Please call 112 police, it is urgent
